title: Wait Times for Pedestrians at Signalised Junctions
what_it_is: Wait Times for Pedestrians at Signalised Junctions

sections.label: Pedestrian waiting times at junctions
sections.summary: Median and maximum pedestrian waiting times at signalised junctions are 120 and 140 seconds, with Friendly Streets junctions under 60 seconds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Speaker, the median and maximum waiting time for pedestrians at signalised junctions are 120 seconds and 140 seconds respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Wait times for pedestrians depend on the nature of road, junction size and configuration, as well as prevailing traffic volume.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For example, waiting times at signalised junctions of Friendly Streets, which we are expanding to every town by 2030, are under 60 seconds.

sections.label: Dynamic traffic light systems
sections.summary: Authorities study configuration and volumes, use dynamic systems tracking traffic, and work on cameras to track pedestrian volume for adjusting timings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We look at the configuration, the volume of pedestrians and traffic, so that we are able to achieve an optimal situation to balance the different needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We do have dynamic systems that are able to track traffic volume.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We are working on a better system where at certain junctions we might want to install cameras at the pedestrian waiting area to track pedestrian volume and whether we are able to build that capability to also incorporate pedestrian data to adjust traffic lights timings dynamically.

sections.label: Customised crossing light timings
sections.summary: Some crossings change faster, low-volume ones stay green for traffic until pressed, and technology data helps customise crossings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For some, it does turn faster; and for some, there are some crossings where the lights do not usually change because it has a very low pedestrian crossing volume.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: And therefore, the lights are green in favour of the traffic, and unless someone presses it and then, it will turn red or have the green man turned on for the pedestrian.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We will customise it for the need of the particular crossing and where possible, we use technology data from the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) 2.0 system to allow us to better assess the different needs and then to achieve a more optimal situation for all.
